newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher after new low set.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher after new low set.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter closed mostly higher amid growing sentiment the market may be bottoming out after earlier sliding to the lowest level for the nearby contract in almost three years.
Dealers said, however, the scope for any significant rally appeared limited as harvesting in Kansas continued to make good progress with heftier yields than expected noted.
"People are pleasantly surprised (by yields)," one dealer said, noting that prospects for the Kansas crop had appeared bleak after a mid-April freeze.
There was talk that by the end of the weekend, 50 percent of the Kansas wheat crop would have been harvested. USDA reported earlier this week that, as of Sunday, the harvest was 15 percent done.
Featured buyers included Cargill Investor Services, LFG and Refco. FIMAT were a noted seller, traders said.
July wheat closed 1/4 cent per bushel higher at $3.31 a bushel after earlier setting a contract low of $3.30, the lowest level for the nearby position since July 1994.
Other months finished 3/4 cent higher to 1/2 cent lower.
